scenes.headline: How Bonsai squeezes a 27B model to about one bit
scenes.sub: PrismML's Bonsai 27B: Qwen3.6-27B, quantized end to end, small enough for a phone.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sorrel! Bonsai takes a twenty-seven-billion-parameter Qwen model and stores each weight in about one bit. Here's how, and what it costs.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Re-encode every weight at close to one bit, including the embeddings, attention and LM head that other schemes keep in FP16.
scenes.mark: including the embeddings, attention and LM head
scenes.say: Re-encode every weight at close to one bit, including the embeddings, attention and output head that other schemes keep at full precision.

scenes.title: End to end, not just the MLPs

steps.note: the usual scheme: squeeze only the MLPs
steps.say: Most low-bit schemes squeeze only the big feed-forward layers, and keep the sensitive parts at higher precision.

steps.note: Bonsai: every block at low bit
steps.say: Bonsai pushes the low-bit format through every block. A model isn't small until its embeddings and head are small too.
Alongside sits a compact four-bit vision tower.

scenes.title: Two encodings, close to one bit each
scenes.say: Each weight becomes a tiny code times a shared number.

parts.note: one FP16 scale shared by a group of weights
parts.say: The scale is one sixteen-bit number shared across a group of weights.

parts.note: ternary: 1.71 effective bits per weight, 5.9 GB
parts.say: The ternary model picks minus one, zero or plus one: one point seven one bits per weight.

parts.note: drop the zero: 1-bit, 1.125 bits per weight, 3.9 GB
parts.say: The one-bit model drops the zero, for one point one two five bits, and three point nine gigabytes.

scenes.title: Model size on disk
scenes.say: So fifty-four gigabytes at FP16 becomes five point nine ternary, or three point nine at one bit: small enough, PrismML says, for a phone.

scenes.title: Kept at 1-bit, by category
scenes.say: The cost is uneven. Math keeps about ninety-six percent. Tool calling and vision keep about eighty-two, losing nearly a fifth.

scenes.text: The hard part is end to end: one-bit embeddings and a one-bit head are what make a 27B model fit a phone.

recap: Every block quantized, embeddings and head too
Math holds; tool calling and vision drop
scenes.say: To recap: tiny codes times a shared scale, pushed through every block, with a cost that lands unevenly.
